passage:
"Mummy, I have to tell you something about my mark sheet."
"What is it, Sangeeta?"
Sangeeta's palms were sweating. She had thought of stuffing the paper into her school bag and saying it had not come. "I got low marks in maths. I was scared to show you."
"Let me see." Gopika read it slowly. "Thank you for telling me at once."
"I made a plan. I will do a page of sums every day and ask Sir to explain fractions again."
"That is a good plan. Shall I sit with you sometimes?"
Sangeeta let out her breath.

qa.q: What did Sangeeta think of doing with the paper before she told her mother?
qa.a: She thought of stuffing it into her school bag and saying it had not come.

qa.q: Why was Sangeeta scared to show the mark sheet?
qa.a: She feared her mother would be disappointed in her, and that fear made her palms sweat.

qa.q: What worked in the way Sangeeta shared her result?
qa.a: She told her mother right away and came with a plan, which kept the fear from growing as it would have if she hid the paper.

qa.q: How might Gopika have felt while reading the mark sheet?
qa.a: Gopika probably felt concerned but chose to stay calm and thank her daughter, and to offer help instead of blame.

grounding: A child dreads showing her mark sheet but shares it early with a calm plan, and the fear shrinks.

passage: Tomas walked out of his Lisbon school with the report card in his backpack like a stone. Maths: a big red 2 out of 5. Dad had been so proud of the last one. On the tram, he imagined Dad's face falling, the long sigh. He thought about hiding the card under his mattress until the end of term. His friend Tariq, beside him, said, 'I hid mine last year. Mum found it in a month. It was ten times worse.' Tomas stared out at the river. At home, before he could lose his nerve, he laid the card on the kitchen table. 'Dad, my maths is bad. I've thought about it. Can I ask Senhora Costa for extra help on Tuesdays?' Dad read it, sighed once, and then pulled out a chair. 'Tell me what went wrong.'

qa.q: What mark did Tomas get in maths?
What was Tomas afraid of on the tram?
qa.a: He was afraid of Dad's disappointment, imagining his face falling and the long sigh.

qa.q: Why did Tomas's approach at home work well?
qa.a: He showed the card early and came with a calm plan, extra help on Tuesdays, instead of hiding it.

qa.q: How might Dad have felt when Tomas showed the card with a plan?
qa.a: Disappointed at first, but reassured by Tomas's honesty, so he sat down to talk.

grounding: A boy dreading his father's disappointment over a report card shares it early with a calm plan instead of hiding it.

passage: Results day, and the school hall buzzed with parents on plastic chairs. Mehak clutched her mark sheet: her worst science mark ever. Ammi would be here in ten minutes for the parent-teacher meeting. Mehak's hands were cold. She pictured Ammi's face when Ma'am read the mark out. 'Just don't show her,' Ayesha whispered. 'Say they haven't come yet.' But Ma'am had the list anyway. Mehak went to the gate and waited. When Ammi arrived, Mehak handed her the sheet before they walked in. 'Ammi, science went badly. I got confused in the electricity chapter. I want to redo those exercises with you on Sundays.' Ammi read it, then looked at her. 'Thank you for telling me first.' They walked in together.

qa.a: She was scared of Ammi's disappointment, picturing her face when Ma'am read the mark out.

qa.q: What did Mehak do instead of hiding the result?
qa.a: Showed Ammi first at the gate and offered a plan to redo the exercises on Sundays.

qa.q: How did Ammi feel about hearing it from Mehak first?
qa.a: Grateful and trusting; she thanked Mehak and walked in with her.

grounding: On results day a girl afraid of her mother's disappointment shows her the mark sheet first, with a plan.
